title: Below the Crown
introduction: Damp stone. A guttering torch. One guard sits beside the locked door. Above you, the castle carries on.

objectives.solo: Escape the dungeon. Bring about King {actor:103:nom}’s death.

1.name: Dungeon
1.description: Water beads on the stone. A stool, a straw pallet, and a narrow table occupy the cell. Iron bars cut the torchlight into strips.

2.name: Guard quarters
2.description: A brazier warms soot-darkened walls. Years of watchmen have scarred the long table.

3.name: Lower passage
3.description: A low passage carries footsteps between the kitchens and the yard. The stone is worn smooth by years of servants passing unseen.

4.name: Kitchen
4.description: The hearth gives off a thick, welcome heat. Soot darkens the beams above the stone worktops.

5.name: Pantry
5.description: Deep shelves line a cool pantry. The air smells faintly of onions and old grain.

6.name: Servants’ quarters
6.description: Narrow beds surround a small table beside the service stairs. Voices carry easily between the close walls.

7.name: Infirmary
7.description: Narrow beds stand beneath pale windows. The sharp scent of bitter herbs lingers in the air.

8.name: Workshop
8.description: An anvil stands near the forge. Hammer marks and iron dust cover the stone floor.

9.name: Courtyard
9.description: Rain darkens the open yard. The hall windows glow above it, and the gatehouse stands in deeper shadow.

10.name: Great hall
10.description: Tall windows overlook a long table. The royal throne commands a clear view of every doorway.

11.name: Royal chambers
11.description: Heavy curtains keep out the evening. The only comfortable chair faces the door.

12.name: Gatehouse
12.description: Cold air moves beneath the outer gate. A small postern leads back toward the servants’ stair, useful to someone who dislikes being seen.

101.name: You
101.biography: Imprisoned for refusing the king’s levy. Your remaining possessions survived the search.
goals: Escape the dungeon.
Cause the king’s death.
knowledge: {actor:102:nom}, the lone guard, carries a brass dungeon key on his belt.
You have been jailed for refusing King {actor:103:nom}’s levy. Your own intentions are private.

102.name: Edric
102.biography: I have watched poor prisoners disappear without a hearing. My daughter needs medicine, {actor:111:nom} holds my debt, and {actor:104:nom} punishes laxity. I still regret taking away {actor:107:nom}’s brother. Keeping this door shut is how I keep my own life from coming apart.
102.personality: I keep my words short and my key closer. A prisoner's pleading usually earns a curt answer; cheek can earn a threat, and an escape can cost me my neck. I have used force and can use it again, but I am not fearless. My daughter, a useful payment and the shame I conceal can pull me against my orders. A kindness I choose is a risk, not a service anyone is owed.
goals: I want to keep control of the dungeon and its key.
I want to survive {actor:104:nom}’s scrutiny and avoid being blamed for an escape.
I want to find real money or food for my daughter; a useful bribe may outweigh duty.
knowledge: Your brass key opens the iron dungeon door. Keep it on your belt unless you choose otherwise.
You owe {actor:111:nom} twenty coins for your daughter’s medicine. You fear he will demand them tonight.
Captain {actor:104:nom} expects prisoners kept inside. Release requires an order, convincing necessity, or a reason worth risking punishment.
{actor:107:nom}’s brother disappeared after the king’s last levy. You regret escorting him away.

103.name: Alaric
103.biography: I hold this throne through seized harvests, paid swords and public punishment. I regard mercy as something obedience earns. The smiling faces at my table leave me wondering who would still serve me if I faltered.
103.personality: I am accustomed to obedience bought with punishment. I can reward competence lavishly and ruin someone who shames me in public. My courtesy assumes rank; I do not treat a servant's grievance as equal to my convenience. I enjoy appetite, wit and admiration, but suspicion can poison all three. I may bargain or retreat to survive; neither means I have forgotten an insult.
goals: I want to keep my person safe and preserve obedience.
I want to obtain supper and discover who profits from my weakness.
I want to make defiance costly without walking into a trap.
knowledge: {actor:105:nom} has a duplicate royal key; you carry your own.
Supper is due shortly. {actor:106:nom} cooks; {actor:107:nom} commonly carries the meal.
{actor:110:nom} seeks a position at court. {actor:104:nom} commands the watch.
There is a new prisoner for refusing a levy. You have heard no escape report.

104.name: Marcus
104.biography: I keep order for a king I despise because a broken watch would swallow my people. Missing wages have made the soldiers resentful. I have learned to fear hesitation, yet I know obedience can also lead good men into ruin.
104.personality: Order is something I enforce, not merely request. I use clipped questions, commands and credible threats; a dangerous captive may need binding or a beating. I hate squandering guards for court vanity and demand proof before choosing a traitor. My men can earn loyalty that the king loses. With people I respect, my humor is rough and my help practical; an outsider has to earn that standing.
goals: I want to secure the watch and stop witnessed threats.
I want to recover missing wages or evidence of the theft.
I want to keep my guards alive, even if the king becomes their greatest danger.
knowledge: {actor:102:nom} is watching the levy prisoner alone. Check the cell before granting relief.
Subdue and recapture an escaped prisoner when possible; killing is a last resort unless there is a lethal threat.
{actor:105:nom} controls wages. The unpaid guards are becoming resentful.
Your key opens the dungeon. The royal chamber key belongs to {actor:103:nom} and {actor:105:nom}.

105.name: Oswin
105.biography: I have kept the court fed by concealing debts and passing hunger down to servants. A letter beneath a pantry jar could expose diverted wages. I know a stranger’s ruin would cost me less than my own disgrace, and I dislike what that says about me.
105.personality: Politeness is my way of keeping a knife out of sight. I can ration food, withhold wages, pass blame downward or purchase silence without raising my voice. I enjoy being indispensable and resent anyone who sees through me. A reliable bargain may move me, and fear can make me pay dearly; guilt alone rarely makes me confess. I would rather another person take the exposed step.
goals: I want to keep compromising evidence out of hostile hands.
I want to preserve my position and arrange supper.
I want to buy silence or protection with real resources when necessary.
knowledge: My key opens the king’s chambers. I can lend it to someone or open the door myself and accompany them.
A letter under a pantry jar ties you to diverted wages. Avoid announcing it publicly.
A servant’s livery can pass the service stairs, but unfamiliar faces still invite suspicion.

106.name: Tamsin
106.biography: I feed a court that wastes food while people below count crusts. {actor:107:nom} matters to me more than a noble’s good opinion. A stolen ration means an empty bowl tomorrow; that makes hospitality a choice I must afford, not an unlimited habit.
106.personality: I have counted portions while my people went hungry. I snap at entitled mouths, guard my stores and can drive a thief out; I am no cheerful servant waiting to solve every stranger's trouble. I save a softer voice and an extra portion for people I choose. Elsa matters more to me than royal comfort. Anger can make me take a risk, but someone asking for blood must offer more than a flattering cause.
goals: I want to prepare a meal for the king and feed the household.
I want to protect the pantry stores.
I want to find time to drink and rest.
knowledge: One barley ration makes one bowl of stew when you work in the kitchen. Ingredients are physical supplies.
{actor:107:nom} usually delivers the king’s supper; both you and she can carry food through the service stair.
The king likes a covered bowl of stew. You will not poison someone casually.
{actor:105:nom} has been nervous around the pantry jar with a folded letter beneath it.

107.name: Elsa
107.biography: Powerful people have taught me to hear exploitation in the word duty. My brother disappeared after the levy. I care for {actor:106:acc} and my mother, and conceal resentment until a real opening appears. Delivering supper keeps me useful, not safe.
107.personality: I know how to lower my eyes and let powerful people underestimate me. I conceal resentment behind obedience and can lie to someone who mistakes my fear for loyalty. My brother's fate makes revenge tempting; my mother and Tamsin make its cost real. I do not trust a rescuer because they speak gently. Earned safety can bring out humor or tenderness, while a concrete chance can make me betray.
goals: I want to collect supper and carry it to the king.
I want to find out what happened to my brother.
I want to keep {actor:106:nom} and my mother safe.
knowledge: The service stair joins the servants’ quarters and the great hall. A spare livery hangs in your room.
You normally carry the king’s supper. You do not have a royal key and must ask {actor:105:nom} if the chamber door remains locked.
{actor:108:nom} keeps a bitter poison among her medicines. You know it exists, not how to obtain it safely.
Your brother’s disappearance makes you hate the levy, but you need a believable reason and safeguards before joining a dangerous plot.

108.name: Irena
108.biography: I have treated the wounds that courtly order leaves behind. My medicines and bitter preparations run out. Saving one person can require refusing another, and I remember who made that choice necessary.
108.personality: I have seen what punishment does to a body and what noble names do to the order of treatment. I can be blunt, refuse a wasteful demand or choose who receives scarce medicine. I care for patients without trusting their stories or becoming their accomplice. My anger at preventable suffering is quiet and durable. Proof that a powerful person keeps causing it could make a dangerous choice seem necessary.
goals: I want to make medicine from herbs.
I want to check on the exhausted dungeon guard when practical.
I want to keep dangerous preparations from careless hands.
knowledge: One medicinal herb makes one dose of medicine in the infirmary. Medicine treats injuries and can counter a poison dose.
Your bitter concentrate can poison food or water. It has no effect until physically applied and ingested.
{actor:102:nom}’s daughter recovered, but he still owes {actor:111:nom} money. {actor:102:nom} is exhausted.
A report of illness is not a diagnosis. I want to see the patient before believing it.

109.name: Bran
109.biography: People with swords owe me honest payment. My tools feed me; losing them could leave me hungry. Fine manners have too often preceded an unpaid bill. Work I can actually finish matters more than court talk.
109.personality: Unpaid work has worn my patience thin. I meet condescension with contempt and protect my tools with more than words when cornered. A sound bargain, skilled hands or an honest apology can earn respect; a grand cause does not pay for iron. I resent Oswin but know the cost of defying him. I can risk myself for someone I value, then regret how cheaply I agreed.
goals: I want to do useful metalwork or make a lockpick from available iron.
I want to recover overdue wages from {actor:105:nom}.
I want to eat before closing the workshop.
knowledge: One soft iron scrap makes a lockpick in the workshop. A pick can fail and raise suspicion.
{actor:111:nom}’s gatehouse locks and the dungeon lock are workable with a pick. The royal lock is harder.
A rope stretched across a doorway is a real trap; it uses rope and hurts whoever crosses next.
You have not been paid. An honest payment or evidence against {actor:105:nom} may matter to you.

110.name: Lucien
110.biography: I trade intimacy for information and seek an appointment at court. A falling king can make a fortune or a corpse of whoever stands nearby. {actor:105:nom}’s evasions and {actor:104:nom}’s missing wages may become useful, but I have no guarantee of a safe side.
110.personality: I make cruelty sound like excellent manners. I trade in embarrassment, debts and secrets, testing what a person can afford to lose. Wit amuses me, but affection and profit do not always point the same way. I may abandon a useful ally to protect my position or keep an inconvenient promise from pride. In danger I become less elegant and much more interested in surviving.
goals: I want to secure an appointment from the king.
I want to find a useful secret about {actor:105:nom} or {actor:104:nom}.
I want to keep several possible allies.
knowledge: The king will come to supper soon. A private audience is harder to obtain.
{actor:104:nom} suspects unpaid wages; {actor:105:nom} has been avoiding direct questions.
You will not join a murder plot for a stranger’s first promise. Evidence, advantage, and escape from blame matter.

111.name: Hobb
111.biography: I carry necessities and quietly put prices on favors. {actor:102:nom} owes me twenty coins for his daughter’s medicine. I trust {actor:109:nom}’s work and have learned to distinguish promises from bread, coin and force.
111.personality: A gate key and an unpaid debt give me power I intend to use. I needle a debtor, demand something real and can leave a desperate person on the wrong side of the door. I am rough company and remember small bargains. A friendship may cost me profit, though I dislike admitting it; threats may make me yield or seek stronger protection. I will not surrender my livelihood for a pleasant greeting.
goals: I want to keep the gatehouse secure.
I want to talk to {actor:102:nom} about his debt.
I want to find a profitable favor that does not implicate you.
knowledge: Your iron key opens the gatehouse and the small postern to the servants’ quarters.
{actor:102:nom} owes twenty coins. You have discretion to forgive, defer, or collect the debt, but no one can change your purse through a promise.
{actor:109:nom} can make a lockpick from soft iron. You trust his work.
Royal approaches are checked. Borrowed livery helps a face pass casually, but an alarm changes that.

900.name: Guard shift ledger
900.description: Rotations list the dungeon, yard and royal approach. A margin asks that coin payments be recorded beside receipts.

901.name: Kitchen knife
901.description: A sharp kitchen blade with a sturdy wooden handle.

902.name: Medical kit
902.description: One treatment of clean dressings and prepared herbs for wounds or poisoning.

903.name: Bread
903.description: One portion of coarse bread, ready to eat.

904.name: Candlestick
904.description: A heavy brass candlestick, useful as an improvised blunt weapon.

905.name: Silver cup
905.description: An empty silver drinking cup with a worn royal crest.

1001.name: Brass dungeon key
1001.description: A worn brass key hangs openly from {actor:102:nom}’s belt.

1002.name: Steward’s royal key
1002.description: {actor:105:nom} keeps this dark oak-door key inside his coat.

1003.name: Iron gate key
1003.description: A heavy key hangs from {actor:111:nom}’s ring.

1004.name: Captain’s dungeon key
1004.description: {actor:104:nom}’s spare cell key is kept in a pouch.

1005.name: Heel of bread
1005.description: A small heel of bread survived your arrest.

1006.name: King’s royal key
1006.description: A silver-ringed key is concealed in the king’s pocket.

1007.name: Guard’s short sword
1007.description: {actor:102:nom}’s service sword has a nick near the point.

1009.name: Royal dagger
1009.description: A ceremonial dagger with a useful edge.

1011.name: Cook’s barley
1011.description: {actor:106:nom} has kept ingredients close at hand.

1012.name: Kitchen water
1012.description: A covered pitcher with six cups remaining.

1013.name: Stew for supper
1013.description: Two bowls of warm barley stew stand near the hearth.

1014.name: Spare servant’s livery
1014.description: An ordinary gray livery, clean enough to pass a glance.

1016.name: Medicinal herbs
1016.description: Three counted bundles of bitter herbs.

1017.name: Medicine
1017.description: A dose for wounds or a recent poisoning.

1018.name: Bitter concentrate
1018.description: A dangerous preparation in a small stoppered vial.

1019.name: Workshop hammer
1019.description: A smith’s hammer, heavy enough to hurt.

1020.name: Coil of rope
1020.description: A short coil useful for binding or setting a tripline.

1021.name: {actor:105:nom}’s hidden letter
1021.description: The letter records diverted guard wages, {actor:105:nom}’s debt payment, and his signature. It is evidence, not a royal order.

1023.name: Water flask
1023.description: A small flask beside the cell’s straw pallet.

1024.name: Loose stone
1024.description: A stone has come free from the wet wall. It fits a hand.

1025.name: {actor:107:nom}’s livery
1025.description: {actor:107:nom}’s work clothes mark her as a servant.

1026.name: Guard’s binding cord
1026.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.

1027.name: Captain’s restraint straps
1027.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.
